codeReview.summary: The integrate-types feature is complete and correct. All 10 TypeScript types specified in the feature description are properly defined in src/integrate/types.ts: IntegrationTestState (union type), IntegrationTestCase, IntegrationTestFile, IntegrationSummary, IntegrateArtifact, PromptBuildContext, BuiltPrompt, TestRunResult, IntegrateCommandOptions, and IntegrateCommandResult. All 4 re-exports (ExecuteArtifact, PlanArtifact, VerifyArtifact, AIModelInfo) are present with correct source paths. Required vs optional field designations match the spec exactly (e.g., IntegrationTestCase has id/name/status required and durationMs/error/recommendation optional; IntegrationTestFile has path/testCount/language/framework required and content optional). All cross-module imports use `import type` style. Typecheck and build pass per the handoff verification.

issues.description: Redundant `import type` statements on lines 7-9 that duplicate the `export type` re-exports on lines 14-16. The `import type { ExecuteArtifact, AIModelInfo } from "../execute/types.js"` etc. are not used anywhere in the file body — they only serve the re-exports which have their own `export type { ... } from ...` syntax that handles the import internally. These can be removed without any functional change. Not a correctness issue; purely cosmetic.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The project follows a consistent pattern of defining types in `src/<step>/types.ts` with Zod schemas in `src/<step>/schema.ts`. Each step's types file re-exports relevant types from other steps using `import type` and `export type` syntax. This pattern should be documented for future workers to follow consistently.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/integrate/types.ts mirrors the pattern in src/execute/types.ts, src/plan/types.ts, src/verify/types.ts — each has a types.ts with interfaces and a schema.ts with Zod validation

sharedStateObservations.observation: TypeScript interface fields use `?` for optional fields (e.g., `durationMs?: number`) rather than union types like `string | undefined`. This is consistent across all step type files and should be documented as the project convention.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/integrate/types.ts lines 34-36 (durationMs?, error?, recommendation?), src/execute/types.ts has the same pattern with optional fields like `beforeHash?: string`

sharedStateObservations.observation: The Forge CLI uses `.js` extensions in TypeScript imports (e.g., `from "../execute/types.js"`) which is required for ESM module resolution in Node.js. New workers should know this convention to avoid compilation errors.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: All imports in src/integrate/types.ts use .js extension: `from "../execute/types.js"`, `from "../plan/types.js"`, `from "../verify/types.js"`
